# Session titles: generated by Claude Code, listed like everywhere else, renamed without a trace

> Language: **English** · [한국어](./ko.md)

## What was reported

In [#562](https://github.com/Swttch/swttch/issues/562) a user wrote that the name of a session in this app is just the beginning of the first message they sent, while in Claude's own apps a session gets a short name made from the conversation. Renaming a session was also a private matter of this app: a name typed in the session dropdown was not seen by Claude Code in the terminal or by its other clients.

Three things changed together, so that a session reads the same wherever you open it.

- A new session gets a **generated title**, as it does in the terminal.
- A session is **listed in the same order of names** that Claude Code's own clients use.
- A name you type in the dropdown is **Claude Code's own session name**, and it adds nothing to the conversation.

## The generated title

Send the first message of a new session. A moment later, while the first answer is still streaming in, Claude Code writes a short title for the session and the header takes it. The title shows up in the header, in the session dropdown and on the session list page.

![The top bar of a chat. The title "Early login session cookie expiry" sits at the left under a folder icon, above the first message "Why do login session cookies expire too early? Answer in one sentence and do not use any tools." and the start of the answer.](./assets/header-generated-title.png)

*The header after the title arrived. Until then it showed the first words of the message.*

![The open session dropdown. Under the search box and the filter row, the heading "Today" is followed by one session row, "Early login session cookie expiry", marked "now".](./assets/dropdown-generated-title.png)

*The same title in the session dropdown.*

What the title is like:

- It is a short noun phrase, two to five words, about what the session is about.
- It is in the language of your conversation. If you set **Settings > General > Language** (Claude's response language), the title follows that language instead.
- It is made once, from your first message. It does not change as the conversation moves on.

### How the title appears

A title that has just been generated is drawn one letter at a time in the header and in the session rows, instead of replacing the first words in a single frame. It takes a second or so, and no more than a second and a half however long the title is. It plays once. A title you typed yourself, a session you reopen and a list you reload show the title as it is. If your system asks for reduced motion, the title appears at once.

### When no title is made

- The first message is a slash command such as `/init`. Claude Code does not name a session after a command, so the session keeps the words it has.
- The first message is very short. If nothing came back, the next messages try again, three tries in all.
- The session was already there before this version, or you reopen an older session. Only a session started in this app, with this setting on, is asked.
- The setting below is off.

If Claude Code cannot be asked, or does not answer, nothing happens: the session is listed under the words it already has, exactly as before. Nothing breaks, and no error is shown.

## How a session is listed

The dropdown and the session list page pick the name of a session from the first of these that it has:

| Order | What | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The name you gave it | **Rename** in the dropdown, or `/rename` in any Claude Code client |
| 2 | The generated title | Claude Code, right after the first message |
| 3 | The latest message you sent in it | The session itself |
| 4 | A summary Claude Code wrote for it | The session itself |
| 5 | The first message | The session itself |

This is the order Claude Code's own clients use, so the same session carries the same name in the terminal, in the editor extensions and in the desktop app. Before this version, steps 2 and 3 were missing here.

## The two settings

Both are in **Settings > General**, next to the other app settings, and both are on by default. Like the rest, each can be set for a project on the project tab.

![Three settings rows. "Paginate chat history" is on. "Generate session titles automatically" with the line "Claude Code names a new session from its first message, as it does in the terminal." is on. "List unnamed sessions by their last prompt" with the line "Sessions with no name or generated title are listed by their last prompt instead of their first." is on.](./assets/settings-rows.png)

*The two new rows, both on.*

- **Generate session titles automatically.** Off, a new session is not asked for a title and is listed under what it already has: the latest message, or the first message if the next setting is off too. Claude Code itself has no switch for this, so the setting belongs to this app alone.
- **List unnamed sessions by their last prompt.** On, a session with no name and no generated title is listed under the latest message you sent in it. Off, it is listed under its summary or its first message, as this app did before. A session that has a name or a generated title is not affected.

Turning either one off changes how the lists read from then on. Nothing is deleted, and turning it back on brings the earlier names back.

## Renaming a session

Hover a session in the dropdown or on the session list page, click the pencil, type the new name and press **Enter**. The new name shows at once.

- **The name is Claude Code's own.** It is saved in the session, so it also shows in the terminal's session picker and in Claude Code's other clients. It used to be kept in a file only this app read.
- **The conversation stays as it was.** Renaming adds no line to the chat, neither a `/rename` command nor an answer to it.
- **A session someone is running gets told.** If the session is open and running, Claude Code is asked directly. If it is not running, a short-lived Claude Code is started just for the rename. That takes a second or two, and the name is already on screen meanwhile. It makes no model call and uses no usage.
- **If it cannot be saved,** the old name comes back on screen, so the name you see is the name that was saved.
- **Names are one line of up to 200 characters.** A line break turns into a space and a longer name is cut, as Claude Code itself does.

If a Claude Code is too old to take the quiet request, the rename is done with the official `/rename` command instead. That works the same, except that the conversation gains the command and its answer, as it would in the terminal.

### Names you typed in an earlier version

A name typed before this version is still shown, for as long as you leave it. Rename the session once more and the new name replaces it everywhere.

## What it does not do

- It does not title sessions that already exist. Their names appear as the list order above gives them.
- It does not change the label of an editor tab in the IDE by itself. The tab takes the new title the way it takes any title change, without the letter-by-letter drawing.
- A title is never made again once it exists. Rename the session to change it.

## Questions

**Why is my session still named after my first message?** Either the first message was a command or very short (see above), the setting is off, or Claude Code did not answer. Send another message and it tries again, up to three times in all.

**Why does the list show my last message?** A session with no name and no generated title is listed under its latest message. Turn off **List unnamed sessions by their last prompt** to see the first message instead.

**Can I get a better title?** Rename the session. Your name always comes first.
